candidates.claim: The PR deletes the `#adaptation_note` that was the only in-tree record of why `Set`/`Finset` pointwise monoid data were marked `noncomputable`, and the PR description is empty, so nothing states what made them computable again (whether lean4#7824 was reverted/adapted or the workaround became unnecessary). The title — "remove `noncomputable` from Set/Finset Monoid instances" — also does not cover the other declarations the diff changes: `Set.one`, `Set.singletonOneHom`, `Set.singletonMulHom`, `Set.singletonMonoidHom` and `Set.involutiveInv`.
candidates.requested_change: Add a PR description saying why the marks are no longer needed (which Lean change/toolchain made these definitions computable again), and retitle the PR so it names the full set of declarations it changes.
candidates.suggested_fix: Add a PR description saying why the marks are no longer needed (which Lean change/toolchain made these definitions computable again), and retitle the PR so it names the full set of declarations it changes.

candidates.claim: `Set.Ioi_disjoint_Iio_same` silently lost its `@[simp]` tag: the base file had `@[simp] theorem Ioi_disjoint_Iio_same` and `@[simp] theorem Iio_disjoint_Ioi_same`, but the tag was replaced by `@[to_dual Iio_disjoint_Ioi_same]`, so neither the original nor its generated dual is in the simp set any more. Every other declaration dualised in this PR keeps its attribute with the `(attr := …)` form (`Iic_disjoint_Ioi`, `Iio_disjoint_Ici`, `Ici_disjoint_Iic`, `iUnion_Iic`, `iUnion_Iio`, all four `iUnion_…_right`), so this is an unintended regression of a public lemma's simp behaviour rather than a deliberate API change.
candidates.requested_change: Use `@[to_dual (attr := simp) Iio_disjoint_Ioi_same]`, which applies `@[simp]` to both the original and the generated dual, or — if the tag is deliberately being dropped — say so in the PR description (which is currently empty).
candidates.suggested_fix: Use `@[to_dual (attr := simp) Iio_disjoint_Ioi_same]`, which applies `@[simp]` to both the original and the generated dual, or — if the tag is deliberately being dropped — say so in the PR description (which is currently empty).

candidates.claim: `Set.Ioi_disjoint_Iio_iff` silently lost its `@[simp]` tag for the same reason as `Set.Ioi_disjoint_Iio_same`: the base file had `@[simp]` on `Ioi_disjoint_Iio_iff` and on the hand-written `Iio_disjoint_Ioi_iff`, whereas the PR writes `@[to_dual Iio_disjoint_Ioi_iff]`, so neither the lemma nor its generated dual is a simp lemma any more — inconsistent with the `(attr := simp)` transfers used for the rest of the file.
candidates.requested_change: Use `@[to_dual (attr := simp) Iio_disjoint_Ioi_iff]`, restoring `@[simp]` on both `Disjoint (Ioi a) (Iio b) ↔ ¬a < b` and its dual, or explain the removal in the PR description.
candidates.suggested_fix: Use `@[to_dual (attr := simp) Iio_disjoint_Ioi_iff]`, restoring `@[simp]` on both `Disjoint (Ioi a) (Iio b) ↔ ¬a < b` and its dual, or explain the removal in the PR description.
